findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain default value, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created afterwards gets that same stale timestamp, so `queued` never reflects when the assignment was actually queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: Task kwargs carry a raw datetime that may not serialize or round-trip
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object, and that dict is passed straight into the Celery `apply_async` kwargs. With a JSON task serializer this raises at enqueue time. If it does serialize, the value arrives as a string, and `from_dict` does not parse it back into a datetime. The result is either a failed outbound sync or an `AssignmentSource` with a wrongly typed `queued`. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. isoformat) and parse it in `from_dict`.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg is passed to every integration's `sync_assignee_outbound`
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` on every integration. Any concrete implementation (Jira, Jira Server, GitHub, GitLab, VSTS, etc.) whose signature lacks `**kwargs` or an explicit `assignment_source` parameter will raise TypeError, and outbound assignee sync will break for that provider. The PR does not update or check those implementations. The value is also already consumed by `should_sync`, so passing it on is unnecessary.

findings.title: New task kwarg breaks old workers during rolling deploy
findings.body: `sync_assignee_outbound` tasks are now enqueued with an `assignment_source_dict` kwarg. Workers still running the previous code will reject these tasks with TypeError (unexpected keyword argument) until the deploy completes. Normally the task signature change is shipped before producers start sending the new kwarg.

findings.title: Cycle is only broken for the originating integration; multi-integration loops remain
findings.body: Outbound sync is suppressed only when the target integration is the source integration. If a group is linked to issues in two sync-enabled integrations (e.g. Jira and GitHub), an inbound change from A is still pushed to B. B's webhook then reassigns in Sentry with source B, which is pushed back to A, and so on. Rapid successive edits can therefore still ping-pong between integrations.

findings.title: Unused `assignment_source` parameter added to abstract `sync_status_outbound`
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller passes it and no status-sync logic uses it. This changes the documented contract for implementers without any effect and suggests status-sync cycles are handled when they are not.
